interpretation: This introduction presents a reusable contour generator rather than a completed RH criterion. For g(z)=1/(a^2-(z-b)^2) on the rectangle with left edge Re z=b, that edge turns the contour integral of log ζ(z)g(z) into the desired vertical-line log-ζ integral with weight 1/(a^2+t^2); after the other three edges vanish as X→∞, residues and generalized Littlewood theory provide a different route to the same contour quantity. The supported conceptual reading is that choosing the kernel designs the boundary functional exposed by the contour, while closing the contour makes that functional accessible to interior analytic accounting. The note says this scheme is then adapted from log-modulus integrals to weighted arg-ζ integrals, but this span does not identify the individual pole or zero terms, establish their signs, or supply the hypotheses that make a later equality equivalent to RH.
source_support: The span explicitly gives g(z)=1/(a^2-(z-b)^2), the rectangle with vertices b±iX and b+X±iX, the left-edge integral, vanishing of the three external-edge integrals as X→∞, and evaluation using residue and generalized Littlewood theorems. It also explicitly announces analogous arg-ζ integrals. Kernel choice as boundary-functional design is an interpretation of those facts; no specific decomposition into zeta-pole and zero corrections is attributed to this span.
nonparaphrase_operation: Reframes the construction as a two-stage design pattern—select a vertical-line observable with a rational kernel, then convert the closed-contour quantity into interior analytic data—and identifies what this representation gains (a reusable bridge between boundary integrals and contour evaluation) and loses (the later criterion's explicit terms, sign control, and equivalence conditions).
speculation_status: Accepted source-local interpretation with its inferential step labeled. Later-context claims about particular poles, zero contributions, their signs, or RH equivalence are excluded; exact formula transcription remains subject to the stated OCR risk.
quality_reason: Accepted after bounded revision: it preserves the concrete kernel, contour, boundary weight, limiting step, and residue/Littlewood mechanism while performing a supported mechanism-level synthesis. It leaves the decay proof, log-branch conditions, contour hypotheses, and all criterion-specific sign and equivalence work as outstanding proof burdens.
